subject: design-technology
title: Ethics in Design
welcome_lead: Who benefits, who pays, who decides?
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: ethical considerations in product design.

concepts.def: Branch of philosophy concerned with right and wrong action.
Anyone affected by a product or design decision.
Design accessible to the widest range of users.
UI design that tricks the user into unintended actions.
Certification ensuring producers receive a fair price.
Mineral whose extraction funds armed conflict (e.g. coltan).

walkthroughs.body_html: Designers consider all stakeholders: users, makers, communities affected by raw-material extraction, future users (when product becomes waste). The hidden stakeholder often pays the highest cost.
Inclusive design (championed by OXO Good Grips; Microsoft Inclusive Toolkit) seeks accessibility across age, ability, language and context. Designing for the margin often improves the mainstream.
Coltan (tantalum), tin, tungsten and gold — '3TG' — are widely sourced from conflict zones. The US Dodd-Frank Act (2010) and EU Conflict Minerals Regulation (2021) impose reporting requirements.
